# DOCTRINE — combat rebalance & the unlock ratchet

*Companion to `DOCTRINE.md`. Everything here is generated by `rebalance.py` (stat files) and
`generate_tree.py` (the ratchet), and verified against `Warzone2100/warzone2100` master.*

---

## 0. The finding that shaped all of this

Before designing anything I diffed the modifier tables across every release from 3.2.3 (2017) to
master. **In nine years there have been three value changes, one of which was reverted two weeks
later.** The 2010-era values are essentially still live, and nobody has ever attempted a systematic
re-derivation of the MP tables.

And there is no written design intent to work from. NoQ, 2013:

> *"We also still don't have any solid vision of desired weapon functions, eg. how exactly should
> flamers be functionally different from machineguns? I have no idea how to go further without that."*

So this document states the intent first, then derives numbers from it.

---

## 1. Counters — make the specialist beat the generalist

### The failure

`ALL ROUNDER` (cannons, rails, Needle, Gauss, Particle Gun) sits **above neutral against every
ground propulsion except cyborgs**: 105 Tracked, 115 Half-track, 120 Hover, 125 Wheeled. Meanwhile
`ANTI TANK` gets 120 vs Tracked.

**The anti-tank specialist beats the generalist by 15% at its own job.** That is not a counter. It's
the forum complaint verbatim, from 2014:

> *"Since cannons are also an all rounder weapon, they [are] effective against structures, units and
> borgs, **making a mix and match pointless**."* — Amzo2000

### The fix

Pull the generalist to neutral-or-below everywhere; push each specialist hard into its own matchup.

**`weaponmodifier.json`** — 36 values changed:

| effect | Half-Trk | Hover | Legged | Lift | Propellor | Tracked | Wheeled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ALL ROUNDER | 115→**100** | 120→**105** | 65→**55** | 40→**45** | 105→**95** | 105→**90** | 125→**110** |
| ANTI PERSONNEL | 50→**45** | 110→**100** | 150→**175** | 60→**55** | 50→**45** | 40→**35** | 100→**95** |
| ANTI TANK | 125→**150** | 90→**100** | 30→**25** | 80→**70** | 120→**130** | **120→175** | 130→**145** |
| ARTILLERY ROUND | 65→**70** | 110 | 130→**140** | 25→**20** | 65 | 30 | 90→**95** |
| BUNKER BUSTER | 40→**35** | 20 | 30→**25** | 30→**25** | 50→**45** | 50→**45** | 30 |
| FLAMER | 100→**105** | 130→**135** | 130→**155** | 25→**20** | 90 | 90→**70** | 110→**120** |

**Result — specialist:generalist ratio against the same target:**

| target | | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tracked | ANTI TANK | 1.14× | **1.94×** |
| Legged | ANTI PERSONNEL | 2.31× | **3.18×** |
| Legged | ARTILLERY ROUND | 2.00× | **2.55×** |
| Wheeled | ANTI TANK | 1.04× | **1.32×** |

### Structures — artillery becomes a siege weapon

`ARTILLERY ROUND` is currently **100 vs HARD** — and 96 of 165 structures are HARD. Artillery is
exactly neutral against the thing it exists to destroy, and *worse* than neutral (20) against
bunkers. A cannon is as good a siege weapon as a howitzer.

**`structuremodifier.json`** — 21 values changed:

| effect | BUNKER | HARD | MEDIUM | SOFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ALL ROUNDER | 75→**60** | 100→**75** | 100→**95** | 130→**125** |
| ANTI PERSONNEL | 50→**30** | 40→**25** | 65→**55** | 160 |
| ANTI TANK | 60→**55** | 25→**30** | 50→**60** | 75→**80** |
| ARTILLERY ROUND | **20→45** | **100→130** | **120→165** | 200 |
| BUNKER BUSTER | 400→**450** | 300→**320** | 120→**130** | 100 |
| FLAMER | 300→**320** | 10→**15** | 60→**65** | 150→**155** |

Mortars and howitzers now genuinely break bases; cannons genuinely don't.

## 2. Armour — the highest-leverage single number in the game

```
combat.cpp:650   final = MAX(modified − armour, modified × minimumDamage/100)
```

`minimumDamage` is a **per-weapon** field. **All 119 designable MP weapons ship at 33.** crab_ found
what that means in 2013:

> *"machineguns are ignoring armor actually (do 33% dmg) … After some point (after first or second
> armor upgrade) **all machineguns just doing minimum 33% damage. That damage does not depend on
> armor. So Machinegun ignore armor.**"*

Dev **Per** replied: *"In 3.2, you can mod the amount percentage of armour ignored, so you can
experiment with that."* **Nobody in MP ever has.**

The key insight: the floor doesn't flatten the modifier table — **it flattens armour**. Once
`armour ≥ 0.67 × modified damage`, damage becomes completely armour-independent. So the floor is
really "how much does this weapon care about plate," and setting it per role is what makes a counter
feel like a counter.

| effect | old | new | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANTI PERSONNEL | 33 | **20** | blunted by armour — that's the point |
| ALL ROUNDER | 33 | **25** | generalist; armour hurts it |
| FLAMER | 33 | **30** | thermal channel |
| ARTILLERY ROUND | 33 | **35** | big shells care less about plate |
| ANTI TANK | 33 | **45** | a penetrator; reliably defeats armour |
| BUNKER BUSTER | 33 | **55** | shaped charge |

**This also makes armour research meaningful again** — currently a third of incoming damage ignores
every armour upgrade you ever buy.

## 3. Salvo — the second missile stops flying at a corpse

### What's actually happening

`WEAPON_TIME = 100` (`stats.cpp:45`), so JSON time values are ×100 to get milliseconds.

| | rounds | round 2 launches | round 1 *lands* |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scourge | 2 | **200 ms** | ~1327 ms |
| Tank Killer | 2 | **100 ms** | ~752 ms |
| Lancer | 2 | **100 ms** | ~677 ms |

The second missile is away **a full second** before the first one arrives. Guaranteed overkill on
anything the first round would have killed.

### Why the fix is small

**The engine does not treat a salvo as atomic.** Each round is an independent `combFire()` decision,
and `ammo` persists across target changes — it only refills once `reloadTime` has elapsed
(`combat.cpp:120–135`). So an unspent round **carries to the next target with zero waste**.

The behaviour you want is already in the architecture. It's suppressed purely because `firePause`
is set to 1–2 ticks. Space the rounds past flight time and the engine does the rest.

| weapon | firePause | reloadTime | full cycle |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scourge | 2 → **14** (1400 ms) | 100 → **86** | 10200 → **10000 ms** |
| Tank Killer | 1 → **8** (800 ms) | 180 → **172** | 18100 → **18000 ms** |
| Lancer | 1 → **7** (700 ms) | 160 → **153** | 16100 → **16000 ms** |

`reloadTime` is trimmed so the **full cycle is unchanged** — sustained DPS into a target that
*survives* round one is identical to vanilla. The only thing that changes is that a target which
dies to round one no longer eats round two.

> **Not touched:** MRL (8 rounds), Sunburst (6), Vindicator (4), Avenger (2). These are saturation
> and AA weapons whose job *is* to blanket a volume. Spacing their rounds would break them.

> **A trap I hit and you should know about:** the cyborg AT weapons (`Cyb-Hvywpn-A-T`,
> `Cyb-Wpn-Atmiss`, `Cyb-Hvywpn-TK`, `CyborgRocket`) *look* like salvo weapons but have **no
> `numRounds` and no `reloadTime`** — `firePause` (80–180, i.e. **8–18 seconds**) is their entire
> firing cycle. Rewriting it would have turned an 8s cycle into 1.2s: a ~7× DPS buff by accident.
> `rebalance.py` now guards on `numRounds > 1`.

## 4. Air — raise the floor, not the ceiling

### The correction I'd push back on

The community verdict is **not** "VTOLs are weak." It's "VTOLs are binary." Zepherian opened a
thread claiming they were unstoppable, benchmarked it himself, and retracted:

> *"AA research is indeed in time with vtol and body research and that it's balanced… **The thing is
> it is a very binary situation.** If you are playing a vtol game… you must research aa asap and you
> must keep upgrading and building it non stop. **There is no mid ground**… AA as an afterthought
> will not work."*

crab_, stated as a hard constraint:

> *"**In current balance we cannot make VTOLs stronger because it will make VTOLs overpowered in
> certain cases.**"*

So a straight damage buff is the wrong instrument — it widens exactly the swing people already hate.
What air needs is a **higher expected value per sortie and a smaller alpha strike**.

### And a fact that kills the obvious fix

`"ANTI AIRCRAFT"` and `"ALL ROUNDER"` are **aliases for the same enum value** (`stats.cpp:1669`):

```cpp
else if (strcmp(weaponEffect, "ANTI AIRCRAFT") == 0 || strcmp(weaponEffect, "ALL ROUNDER") == 0)
{ *effect = WE_ANTI_AIRCRAFT; }
```

There are exactly six weapon effects and no free slot. Every dedicated AA weapon is tagged
`ANTI TANK`, so **AA and ground anti-tank cannot be separated via the modifier table at all**. Any
"give AA its own row" plan is dead on arrival. AA has to be tuned per weapon.

### The changes

**(a) VTOLs survive to deliver.** `V-Tol` propulsion has `hitpointPctOfBody: 100` — *identical to
Wheels*, while Tracks get 300 and Half-tracks 200.

```
V-Tol / Helicopter   hitpointPctOfBody   100 → 150
```

This raises the *floor* of a sortie (it arrives and drops its payload) far more than the ceiling.

**(b) Fix the payload asymmetry.** Missile VTOLs get **2 shots per sortie**; VTOL Assault Gun gets
**36**. That is the single most lopsided number in the air game.

| | attack runs | shots/sortie |
|---|---|---|
| VTOL Lancer | 1 → **3** | 2 → **6** |
| VTOL Tank Killer | 1 → **2** | 2 → **4** |
| VTOL Scourge | 1 → **2** | 2 → **4** |
| VTOL Bunker Buster | 1 → **2** | 2 → **4** |

**(c) Hand the difference back to dedicated AA.** `ANTI TANK vs Lift` drops 80 → 70, which helps
VTOLs against dedicated AA *and* incidental ground fire. Since only dedicated AA should be the
answer, that weapon class gets it back directly:

Hurricane/Whirlwind +15%, Cyclone/Tornado +20%, Sunburst +15%, Avenger/Vindicator +10%,
Stormbringer +10%.

Net: **stray ground fire stops shredding aircraft; committing to AA still stops them.** That is the
"mid ground" Zepherian said doesn't exist.

## 5. The unlock ratchet

Replaces the crew/materiel split from `DOCTRINE.md` §1. This is a better throttle and a better
feeling, and it's the structure you described.

### The rule

Every weapon family has **four axes** — Damage, Range, Reload, Accuracy — and **four tiers**.

1. Combat **unlocks** one random eligible `(axis, tier)` at a time.
2. Power **researches** it.
3. Tier *T* only becomes eligible once **every axis of tier *T−1* has been researched** — not merely
   unlocked.

```
fight ─▶ Range I unlocked ─▶ pay for it (or don't)
fight ─▶ Damage I unlocked ─▶ …
   … all four tier-I topics RESEARCHED ─▶ tier II becomes eligible
```

### Why it works

- **Combat alone cannot run away with the game.** Advancing a tier *requires* spending power. The
  ratchet is its own snowball brake — it does the job the crew/materiel gate was doing, more simply.
- **You cannot rush one axis.** Progress is breadth-first by construction, so every weapon improves
  along all four dimensions instead of becoming a damage number with a gun attached.
- **No two games hand you the same weapon in the same order.** The tree is written by the match.

### How it's expressed

Two of the three rules are **native** `requiredResearch`; only the cross-axis sync needs the script,
and it needs it exactly once per family per tier:

```json
"R-Wpn-Cannon-Range02": {
  "requiredResearch": ["R-Wpn-Cannon-Range01", "R-Cred-Cannon-Tier2"],
  "results": [{"class":"Weapon","filterParameter":"ImpactClass","filterValue":"CANNON",
               "parameter":"MaxRange","value":7}, …]
}
```

`R-Cred-Cannon-Tier2` is a synthetic 10-point marker the script enables once all four Cannon tier-1
topics are **researched**. Everything downstream is ordinary prerequisites, so the research UI,
tooltips and prerequisite display all work with no special-casing.

### The value ladders

Solved so the **relative** gain is constant per tier (the engine adds on the base, so a constant
`value` decays):

| axis | per-tier values | total |
|---|---|---|
| Damage | 25, 31, 39, 49 | **+144%** |
| Reload | 10, 11, 12, 13 | **+46%** rate of fire |
| Accuracy | 10, 11, 12, 13 | **+46%** |
| Range | 7, 7, 8, 9 | **+31%** |

Knowledge to unlock each tier: **800 / 1,680 / 3,528 / 7,409**.
Research cost per tier: **900 / 2,400 / 5,200 / 10,000** points.

### Tree size

| kind | topics | points |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ratchet (11 families × 4 axes × 4 tiers) | 176 | 814,000 |
| Signature (one specific weapon) | 46 | 41,400 |
| Credentials (synthetic markers) | 37 | 370 |
| Penetration | 10 | 100,000 |
| Chassis handling | 9 | 25,500 |
| Command spine | 8 | 40,200 |
| Infrastructure | 8 | 54,800 |
| **Total** | **294** | **1,076,270** |

Validated: acyclic, zero dangling prerequisites, every class/parameter pair checked against
`getUpgradesObject()`, every `filterValue` checked against a real component.

Vanilla: 390 topics / 3,590,910 points. **Visible at any moment here: roughly 4–8 per family you
actually fight with**, because un-enabled topics are invisible.

## 5a. Kill valuation — and a correction to DOCTRINE.md §3.1

> *"Higher tech units should help with the unlock faster if they are killed than lower tech units,
> and if they are really low they should do 0."*

### The correction

`DOCTRINE.md` §3.1 said: don't track anything, just read `commander.experience`. That was right for
an unweighted design and it is **wrong for this one**, for two reasons.

**1. The engine has already flattened the information.** By the time XP lands on the commander it is
a scalar. There is no way to ask what it came from.

**2. The engine has already applied its own weighting, and it is clamped exactly where it matters.**
`qualityFactor()` (`projectile.cpp:301`) scales XP by victim-vs-attacker cost and build points —
then does:

```cpp
CLIP(powerRatio,  65536/2, 65536*2);
CLIP(pointsRatio, 65536/2, 65536*2);
```

**A 0.5 floor.** Killing a scavenger trike with a Gauss tank still pays half. *"Really low should do
zero"* is precisely what that clamp forbids, and it is C++ — a data mod cannot lift it.

So knowledge is computed from a **script-side kill ledger** instead. `eventDestroyed` does not name
the killer, so the standard workaround applies: `eventAttacked(victim, attacker)` maintains a
last-hitter map and the kill is credited on destroy.

**What changes:** `commander.experience` stops being the knowledge meter and reverts to being purely
the rank mechanic — which still drives group size and combat bonuses, so it still matters. The
commander remains the accumulator and the courier: unbanked knowledge rides with it, and is lost or
black-box recovered on death exactly as designed. Only the meter changes.

### The value metric

`droid.cost` is exposed to JS (`quickjs_backend.cpp:1514` → `calcDroidPower`) and returns the summed
component build cost. A Dragon/Gauss/Tracks costs **602**; a scavenger trike costs **38**. That ratio
*is* the tech gap — no separate "tech level" concept needs inventing.

### The reference — and why p75

Weight is relative to **your own army**, so it self-scales. The Viper that was a fair fight at minute
five is worth nothing by minute forty, with nothing to retune.

Reference = the **75th-percentile cost of your own active combat droids**.

- **Not the mean** — fielding a screen of cheap junk would drag the bar down and inflate the value of
  everything you kill.
- **Not the attacker's own cost** (which is what the engine uses) — that rewards sniping with the
  cheapest possible unit.
- p75 can only be lowered by actually giving up your good units. That isn't an exploit, it's a
  sacrifice.

### The curve

```
r = target cost / your p75

r < 0.40            → 0            nothing to learn from something this far beneath you
0.40 ≤ r < 1.00     → ramp 0 → 1
1.00 ≤ r < 2.50     → ramp 1 → 2.5
r ≥ 2.50            → 2.5          cap
```

### What it does across a game

| target killed | cost | early (ref 62) | mid (ref 285) | late (ref 480) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scavenger trike | 38 | 0.35× | **nothing** | **nothing** |
| Viper MG half-track | 62 | 1.00× | **nothing** | **nothing** |
| Cobra Light Cannon | 155 | 2.50× | 0.24× | **nothing** |
| Cobra Lancer | 230 | 2.50× | 0.68× | 0.13× |
| Python Medium Cannon | 285 | 2.50× | 1.00× | 0.32× |
| Tiger Heavy Cannon | 409 | 2.50× | 1.44× | 0.75× |
| Vengeance Scourge | 480 | 2.50× | 1.68× | 1.00× |
| Dragon Gauss | 602 | 2.50× | 2.11× | 1.25× |

Scavengers teach you something while you're in Vipers, and nothing once you're in Pythons. By the
time you field Vengeance hulls, even a Cobra Light Cannon is beneath notice. The anti-farming rule
falls out of the same curve that produces the reward for punching above your weight — it is one
function, not a rule plus an exception.

**Side effect worth having:** this kills grinding as a strategy. You cannot farm a scavenger base for
an hour to unlock the tree. Knowledge only comes from fights that were actually worth having.

## 6. What needs playtesting before you trust it

| Concern | Status |
|---|---|
| **Kill-ledger accuracy.** `eventDestroyed` doesn't name the killer, so credit relies on a last-hitter map from `eventAttacked`. Splash, artillery and simultaneous fire will misattribute some kills. | Acceptable — it only shifts *which* of your own units gets credit, and knowledge pools at the commander anyway. Set a short staleness window (~4s) so a unit that wandered off and died later isn't credited. |
| **p75 is recomputed continuously.** A player who loses their heavy units mid-fight briefly gets a lower reference and inflated weights. | Smooth it over ~30s, or take p75 of units *built*, not units alive. |
| **AP vs heavy armour may now be too dead.** Assault Gun vs an upgraded tracked Python lands ~2.3 damage/shot (was 4.4). The specialist:generalist *ratio* looks enormous (131×) only because the denominator is tiny — but the absolute number is what matters, and it may be past "bad counter" into "not a weapon". | **Dial:** `ANTI PERSONNEL` minimumDamage (20) and vs-Tracked (35). Raise both a step if MG play feels dead. |
| ANTI TANK 175 vs Tracked is the largest single jump here. | Watch for AT becoming the only correct opener. Cyborgs (AT vs Legged = 25) are the intended check. |
| VTOL survivability +50% stacks with +payload. | If air feels oppressive, cut the payload change first — it raises alpha; the HP change raises the floor. |
| Artillery vs HARD 100→130 with splash. | Base-cracking may be too fast. Check against defended bases, not open field. |
| The ratchet's four-axis sync may feel slow early. | Knowledge base (800) and growth (2.1) are one line in `CONFIG`. |

Nothing here is finely tuned — it's derived from a stated intent, which is more than the shipped
tables have. Treat the numbers as a starting position, not an answer.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `killvalue.py` | The kill-valuation curve, the reference-point tables, and `out/killvalue.json` for the browser. |
| `rebalance.py` | Emits modified stat files as reviewable diffs; prints every change and a counter-sharpness table. |
| `out/stats/weaponmodifier.json` | 36 changes |
| `out/stats/structuremodifier.json` | 21 changes |
| `out/stats/weapons.json` | minimumDamage by role, salvo spacing, air payload, AA compensation |
| `out/stats/propulsion.json` | VTOL survivability |
| `generate_tree.py` | The ratchet — 294 topics as a function of ~20 numbers |
| `validate.py` | DAG + engine-schema validation. Run on every change. |
